annotations.title: Extract open map data for an area

description: Use this when the user wants open geographic data for an area anywhere in the world: buildings, places, roads, addresses, administrative divisions, land use, points of interest, waterways, water areas, power lines, boundaries, railways, routes, transit stops or protected areas. The area is a bbox, a place, or a place with a radius. Returns the count, sample attributes, a map and a file (GeoJSON, KML, Shapefile zip or CSV) with its licence. One extract holds at most 20,000 features: for a town centre use a radius of about 1 km, for dense cities less. For one kind of place (pharmacies, schools, supermarkets) or land (forest, vineyards), set kind. One theme per call: extract the layers the user asks for; when they ask what data exists for a project, name the useful themes and let them choose before extracting several. Data: Overture Maps and OpenStreetMap. Never use the user's current location unless they type it. Give the place as the user names it (place name, address or coordinates): this tool locates it, so find_places is not needed first. Download links build their file when opened; no file is saved. Never pass these links to open_gis_file: list every format the user needs in formats, in this one call.

area.description: The area: a bbox, or a place (name, address or coordinates) with an optional radius in metres. The place the user asks about, not the user's own location.

bbox.description: [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees (WGS 84).

place.description: A place name or address, or a point.

radius_m.description: Radius around the place in metres.

kind.description: Keep only some kinds of feature, matched against their OpenStreetMap tag value in English: pharmacy, school, supermarket, restaurant, hospital, farmland, forest, vineyard. One kind, or several in one call (["forest", "meadow", "grass"]). Leave out for all of the theme.

name: extract_open_data

downloads.description: Download links; each builds its file when opened.

hint.description: What to do next, on errors only.

sources.description: Data sources and licences of the result.
